createinteroperable.configuration.title: Create: Interoperable Configuration
createinteroperable.configuration.refurb: ON by default. Refurbished Furniture sinks / baths / toilets no longer fill for free: right-click bare-handed to pull water from an adjacent supply (a tank, a drum, a Create pipe end) into the fixture; hold to keep filling. This overrides Refurbished Furniture's own dispenseWater option. Set false to restore Refurbished Furniture's behaviour.
Millibuckets drawn into the fixture per right-click.
createinteroperable.configuration.sink.r: ON by default. Let's Do sinks (Farm & Charm / Candlelight / Bakery / Alpine Whispers) and the Alpine Whispers bathtub no longer fill for free. Farm & Charm-style sinks: pipes (Create, or any mod exposing a fluid handler on the bottom face) feed an internal buffer; the player fills the basin by right-clicking the faucet when the buffer holds at least fillCostMb. Alpine Whispers sink and bathtub: pipes feed the fixture (sink: bottom or back; bathtub: any side of the tap end except the top) and the tap only runs while that water lasts, closing itself when it runs dry; the bathtub also drinks from a tank it touches. A no-op unless one of those mods is installed. Set false to restore their vanilla behaviour.
createinteroperable.configuration.sink.b: Capacity of the sink's internal supply buffer, in millibuckets.
createinteroperable.configuration.sink.f: Millibuckets drawn from the buffer each time the player fills the basin. An Alpine Whispers basin fills in three steps, each costing a third of this.
createinteroperable.configuration.sink.a: Also let players top up the buffer by hand with a filled bucket.
createinteroperable.configuration.bathtu: Millibuckets of water a full Alpine Whispers bathtub takes, drawn evenly while its tap runs.
createinteroperable.configuration.urbanD: ON by default. Urban Decor sinks, faucets and showers no longer run on nothing: Create pipes (back of the fixture, plus the bottom of a sink or faucet and the top of a shower) feed them, a faucet or shower also drinks from a tank it touches, and a tap that runs dry turns itself off. A no-op unless Urban Decor is installed.
Millibuckets per second a running sink or faucet draws.
Millibuckets of water a toilet's cistern holds (Refurbished Furniture's holds one bucket). Pipes, buckets and bottles fill it; flushing needs it non-empty.

Millibuckets of water a whole bathtub (both halves) holds; Refurbished Furniture's bath holds ten buckets. Pipes into either half, buckets and bottles fill it; the tub has no tap, so it simply fills while water runs in.
Sitting in a bathtub that is at least 40% full washes every harmful effect off.
Seconds one washing machine cycle runs (it pauses while unpowered).
Millibuckets of water one washing machine cycle uses, taken when it starts. Piped in through any side but the top and the door.
Percent of its full durability each damaged item regains from a washing machine cycle (every curse on it is removed as well).
createinteroperable.urban_washer.tip_pow: Power rocker: I readies the machine, O switches it off (and cancels a cycle).
createinteroperable.urban_washer.tip_sta: START: starts a cycle when the machine is ready (on, powered, loaded, and with water); press again to cancel.

createinteroperable.appliance.steam_radi: A small _Steam Hearth_. Burns steam from a pipe on its back and warms the enclosed room around it at half a Hearth's strength. It melts ice and snow, and cats like it.
createinteroperable.appliance.lantern.su: Lights only while _powered_, with light rays like the Streetlight's.
createinteroperable.appliance.lantern.ne: Draws _6 W_ from a Power Kit.

createinteroperable.appliance.fan.summar: A _Create_ fan at a fixed _16 RPM_: it pushes entities and processes items in its air stream. Click to switch it on.
createinteroperable.appliance.washer.sum: Washes wearables: removes their _curses_ and repairs them a little.
createinteroperable.appliance.washer.nee: Needs piped _water_ and a Power Kit (_500 W_).
createinteroperable.appliance.dryer.summ: Dries wearables and adds _Protection I_ to armor that can take it, keeping its other enchantments.
createinteroperable.appliance.dishwasher: Takes tools and weapons: adds _Efficiency I_ to tools and _Unbreaking I_ to weapons. It accepts only what it can improve.
Needs piped _water_ and a Power Kit (_500 W_).

Needs a Power Kit (_750 W_). The switch in its screen turns it off.
createinteroperable.appliance.stove.need: Needs a Power Kit (_1500 W_). The switch in its screen turns it off.
createinteroperable.appliance.fridge.sum: A _water bottle_ left inside slowly turns into a random good potion (3 to 5 minutes).
createinteroperable.appliance.freezer.su: Takes only food, bottles and buckets of water. While running, a _water bucket_ slowly turns into ice and a _water bottle_ into Fire Resistance (3 to 5 minutes).
createinteroperable.appliance.toilet.sum: Sitting on it cures _poison_ and food poisoning. A glass bottle used on it brings back a random foul potion: Poison, Weakness or Oozing.
createinteroperable.appliance.shower.sum: Washes harmful effects off whoever stands under it and gives a little regeneration.
createinteroperable.appliance.bathtub.su: Sitting in it washes harmful effects away. Sneak with an empty hand to pull the plug.
createinteroperable.urban_washer.tip_run: RUN lamp: green while a cycle runs. The same lamps light up on the machine itself.
createinteroperable.urban_washer.tip_pow: POWER lamp: red while switched on and powered by a Power Kit, dim red with no power.
createinteroperable.urban_washer.accepts: Takes tools and weapons. A cycle washes them (curses off, part of the wear repaired) and adds Efficiency I to tools or Unbreaking I to weapons, where it fits.
Takes anything you wear. A cycle adds Protection I where the item can take it.
Takes anything you wear (armour, elytra, heads). A cycle removes curses and repairs part of the wear.
createinteroperable.configuration.urbanD: Millibuckets per second a running shower draws.
Millibuckets a glass bottle takes from a running tap.
A running shower washes every harmful effect off whoever stands under it.
A running shower also gives whoever stands under it a gentle Regeneration.
ON by default. Let's Do Furniture / Candlelight lamps and street lanterns, Alpine Whispers fairy lights, Another Furniture lamps, and Iden's Decor Wall Lamp / Flood Lamp / Floodlight / Fluorescent Light Block become Crayfish electricity consumers: unwired or unpowered = dark, and a lit lamp draws 3 W (12 V). Right-click (Another Furniture) or sneak-right-click (Let's Do) toggles a lamp's switch. A no-op unless one of those mods is installed. Set false to hand every lamp straight back to its own mod (no block entity attached); Another Furniture lamps also regain their redstone response. Also makes new Iden's Decor lights (Pliers-configurable) place in their Refurbished mode when Refurbished Furniture is installed.
createinteroperable.configuration.beachp: ON by default. Let's Do Beachparty's Radio and Mini Fridge become Crayfish electricity consumers: the Radio only plays while powered (10 W, 12 V, billed only while a track plays) and the Mini Fridge only ferments while powered (85 W, 120 V, billed whenever linked). A no-op unless Beachparty is installed. Set false to restore their vanilla behaviour.
createinteroperable.configuration.biblio: ON by default. Bibliocraft's Fancy Crafter no longer auto-crafts from redstone alone: it needs a live rail from a Domestic Electrical Board (100 W, 120 V), billed only while it has a recipe staged. The menu and hopper automation are never blocked, even unpowered. A no-op unless Bibliocraft is installed. Set false to hand it straight back to Bibliocraft's own redstone behaviour.

ON by default. Caps Bibliocraft's Fancy Lantern (every gold/iron, clear/colored, regular/soul flavor) at a vanilla Soul Lantern's light level (10) at most — the 'regular' flavors otherwise register at a full 15, matching vanilla's own Lantern. A no-op unless Bibliocraft is installed. Set false to restore Bibliocraft's own light levels.
createinteroperable.configuration.crnDis: ON by default. A freestanding Create Train Navigator Advanced Display renders its texts only while a live rail from a Domestic Electrical Board reaches it (8 W, 12 V); unwired or unpowered = blank screen. Wiring any one block of a multi-block board powers the whole board. Super-Glued displays and displays built onto a moving contraption or train need no power. A no-op unless Create Train Navigator is installed. Set false to hand displays back to Create Train Navigator (no node attached).
createinteroperable.configuration.vistaT: ON by default. A Vista (cameramod) TV — single or grown into a connected N x N wall — becomes a Domestic Electrical Board electricity consumer instead of a plain redstone lamp: no live rail = always off, no matter what redstone signal reaches it. Once a rail reaches it, it is on by default with NO redstone needed; redstone is repurposed as a manual kill switch that forces the screen off without cutting power. Billed only while actually on (8 W per tile, 12 V, n^2 for a grown wall). A no-op unless Vista is installed. Set false to hand every TV straight back to Vista's own redstone-only behaviour.
createinteroperable.configuration.idenCo: ON by default. Iden's Decor's Computer becomes a Domestic Electrical Board electricity consumer: it only shows an inserted floppy disk's text while a live rail reaches it (15 W, 12 V, billed only while a disk is in). Disks still insert and eject unpowered. A no-op unless Iden's Decor is installed. Set false to hand the computer straight back to Iden's Decor.
createinteroperable.configuration.mtsAaS: PURELY EXPERIMENTAL: patches Immersive Vehicles internals, untested in real play, and may break on any Immersive Vehicles update. ON by default. An Immersive Vehicles (MTS Official Content Pack) AA Base Plate placed on the ground gets a power terminal on one corner, wireable to a Domestic Electrical Board like any appliance. The AA Spotlight mounted on it only lights its beam, auto-rotates or traverses while a live rail reaches the plate: 6 kW on the 120 V rail while lit (+5% while auto-rotating), so it needs a heavy supply. Unpowered, it stays dark and still and shows "Missing power". Spotlights on vehicles, and the AA guns, are untouched. A no-op unless Immersive Vehicles is installed. Set false to hand the Spotlight straight back to Immersive Vehicles (no power needed).
createinteroperable.configuration.mtsPol: PURELY EXPERIMENTAL: patches Immersive Vehicles internals, untested in real play, and may break on any Immersive Vehicles update. ON by default. Every Immersive Vehicles pole block and Signal Controller becomes a wireable Domestic Electrical Board node (a bare pole is a free wire junction; the Signal Controller draws nothing for now). Street lights, flashing signals, traffic and crossing signals mounted on a pole only light while a live rail reaches that pole block: unpowered, every lamp on them is dark and street lights stop lighting the world. 100 W per street-light-type component, 25 W per traffic-signal-type component, on the 120 V rail. Signs are untouched. A no-op unless Immersive Vehicles is installed. Set false to hand every pole light straight back to Immersive Vehicles (no power needed).
createinteroperable.configuration.aircon: A no-op unless Create: Pipes n Physics is installed. With it, the Aircon Motor acts as its own pump: the cold-air face pushes cold air out and the hot-air face sucks hot air in, so an AC loop needs no pumps along its pipes. This is the pump strength at full power, on Pipes n Physics' Create-RPM scale (256 = the fastest a Mechanical Pump turns). It scales down with the motor's power. 0 disables it and leaves the motor as a plain tank.
createinteroperable.configuration.temper: Temperature Mods should affect Power Grid and Electro Energetics devices. OFF by default. When on, and a temperature mod (Cold Sweat) is installed, the temperature around a Power Grid or Electro Energetics device is the temperature mod's: devices in hot places overheat sooner and devices in cold places have more headroom (Power Grid's Thermometer shows the same). When off, both mods use their own heat models as if no temperature mod were installed. Cold Sweat's effects on players (heaters, radiators, aircon) are not affected.
Enable Steam Hearth and Air Conditioning even without Cold Sweat

ON by default. When no temperature mod (Cold Sweat) is installed, the Steam Hearth and the Aircon parts stay craftable and in the creative tab; they work as steam and air machines but change no temperature. Set false to withhold them unless a temperature mod is installed. The Steam Outlet is always available. Blocks already placed keep working either way. Takes effect when a world is next loaded.
createinteroperable.configuration.teleph: A no-op unless Simple Voice Chat is installed. While a telephone call is answered, players speaking near either phone are heard from the other one. Set false to turn the relay off.
Blocks around a phone in which a player's voice is picked up and carried down the line. Whispering picks up half this distance.
Blocks around the far phone within which the carried voice can be heard. A phone is a small speaker: 8 at most (other sounds from a phone always carry 8 blocks).
A faint hiss with the odd soft crackle, played from both phones for as long as a call is answered - mild by default. 0 turns it off, 1 is roughly four times as loud as the default.

createinteroperable.inverter.name: CIO Inverter
createinteroperable.inverter.item.summar: Turns Electro Energetics DC into real three-phase AC: L1-L3 on top, neutral on the side, DC in underneath, and a data pin for a computer.
createinteroperable.inverter.node.neutra: Neutral (AC star point; ground it with a Ground Rod)
createinteroperable.inverter.screen.lamp: RUN: lit while the inverter is putting out AC.
LIMIT: the load asks for more than %s kW (or a phase for more than its share); the output voltage is held down to stay within it.
TRIP: a short held the output down for 3 seconds and it tripped. Switch it on again to reset.
createinteroperable.inverter.screen.freq: Frequency: %s Hz. Drag or scroll (shift: 10 Hz, ctrl: 0.1 Hz). Multiples of 10 Hz fit whole half-cycles into every game tick, so Electro Energetics' meters read a steady voltage; 40 Hz is a CEE alternator turning at 256 RPM.
createinteroperable.inverter.screen.outp: Output: follows the DC input (120 V DC gives 120 V per phase). Turn the knob to regulate it to a set voltage instead.
Output: held at %s V per phase (%s V between phases) by a tap regulator, as long as the DC input is at least that. Scroll for common voltages (shift: 10 V, ctrl: 1 V).
createinteroperable.inverter.screen.sequ: Phase sequence: ABC, or ACB with L2 and L3 swapped (a three-phase motor runs the other way; match it to an alternator before tying them together).
createinteroperable.inverter.screen.swit: On/off: switches the output (a contactor). Switching on also resets a trip.
createinteroperable.inverter.screen.scop: Phasor diagram: each phase's voltage as an arrow, L1 straight up, each later phase 120° behind it, clockwise.
createinteroperable.inverter.screen.wave: The three phases' waveforms, slowed down to one cycle a second so they can be watched.
createinteroperable.inverter.screen.load: L1 %s, L2 %s, L3 %s. Rated %s kW; beyond it the inverter limits its output.
createinteroperable.inverter.screen.capp: This server's Electro Energetics micro-tick setting is too low for the set frequency: running at %s Hz instead.
createinteroperable.inverter.state.rever: DC input reversed: swap DC+ and DC-
createinteroperable.inverter.state.overv: DC input over 1000 V: shut down
createinteroperable.inverter.state.tripp: Tripped by a short: switch on to reset
createinteroperable.urban_cooker.tip_pow: Power rocker: I switches it on (it cooks while a Power Kit powers it, no fuel needed), O switches it off.
createinteroperable.inverter.item.summar: The CIO Inverter in a synchroscope's case: L1-L3 on the top rail, DC-, ground and DC+ on the bottom rail, a data pin on the side for a computer.
createinteroperable.inverter.node.ground: Ground (the phases' star point; wire a Ground Rod to it)
createinteroperable.inverter.screen.phas: Each phase row: volts to neutral | volts to the next phase (L1-L2, L2-L3, L3-L1), then amps. Between phases is about 1.73 times the phase voltage.
